answer: The registry admits at most four identities per autonomous system per epoch. A newcomer submits a signed traceroute from a registrar probe, and a second probe abroad must confirm the same origin ASN within 15 ms of expected jitter. Admission pins the key to that ASN for 30 epochs, and any collision burns a 20 token bond. A 10,000 clone swarm needs 2,500 distinct ASNs, costing roughly $4,200 monthly in residential proxy leases, 600 hours of orchestration, and 200,000 bonded tokens at risk. Each ASN is a basalt bridge pier rated for four raven nests, and a fifth cracks the span.
